title: Opinion dynamics: Statistical physics and beyond
publisher: arXiv (Starnini, Baumann, Galla, Garcia, Iñiguez, Karsai, Lorenz, Sznajd-Weron)

key_points.claim: Review organizes opinion-dynamics models by macroscopic phenomena (consensus, fragmentation, polarization, echo chambers, network coevolution) and by microscopic mechanisms (assimilation, distancing, homophily, etc.).
key_points.evidence_quote: We then categorize models by the macroscopic phenomena they describe (e.g., consensus, polarization, echo chambers) and the microscopic mechanisms of opinion change they encode (e.g., homophily, assimilation).

key_points.claim: Frontier: LLM-based AI agents are being built as testbeds for novel social phenomena. This is covered in Sec. VI.B, which is missing from the fetched text.
key_points.evidence_quote: the recent developments in building artificial intelligence agents as testbeds for novel social phenomena

key_points.claim: LLM agents could let models handle rich textual opinions, which traditional opinion-dynamics models have largely not addressed.
key_points.evidence_quote: with the increasing integration of large language models (LLMs) as agents, future models may begin to process and interact with opinions in this textual format

key_points.claim: Feed-algorithm interventions change how people interact, so agent-based models are needed to predict their effects.
key_points.evidence_quote: This calls for agent-based models that can better predict the effects of these interventions (Garcia, 2023).

key_points.claim: Empirical grounding: experiments support bounded confidence. Perceived closeness to a peer predicted convergence, and extended discussion reduced polarization.
key_points.evidence_quote: extended discussions, unlike short texts, can reduce polarization by narrowing opinion gaps. The study found that perceived closeness to a peer predicted opinion convergence, supporting the bounded confidence principle.

key_points.claim: Lab experiments on conformity closely mirror the q-voter model and can serve as a basis for developing it further.
key_points.evidence_quote: This scheme is almost identical to the q-voter model of opinion dynamics (Castellano et al., 2009b)

key_points.claim: The review scopes out cultural dynamics, language dynamics and human dynamics. It covers analytical and computational methods (stochastic processes, simulation, optimization).
key_points.evidence_quote: Many fields are related to opinion dynamics but are not covered here, such as cultural dynamics

reliability_notes: Full-text PDF, but the fetched text was truncated at about 107k characters, in the empirical section (Sec. III). Sec. IV–VI, including the LLM-agent discussion, were not retrieved. The paper is a review by well-known authors, not a primary study. It is about opinion dynamics, so it covers only one aspect of artificial societies.
